## Dispatch tensor kernels by device (`CUDA`) {#sec-ch01-dispatch}

### Summary

Most of snapy is written as tensor operations that run wherever the tensor lives. The custom kernels, the parts
written by hand for speed, go through a dispatch stub. Each stub is one declared operation with a CPU implementation,
a CUDA implementation when the build has CUDA, and in a few cases an MPS[^rg-a202870e5a6b] one. This section shows that stub for one
operation, the hydrostatic reference, and the two kinds of CUDA loop the kernels use.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: one stub per custom kernel, one registration per device it supports.

**Data.** In: tensors on the caller's device. Out: the same operation by the kernel registered for that device.

**Placement.** At every custom-kernel call; registrations are made at build and load time.

**Activation.** CMake `CUDA` (default OFF) compiles the CUDA kernels; `DEVICE` (default `cpu`) picks the device.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; a kernel without a registration for the requested device fails at dispatch.

**Evidence.** `test_weno5_cuda_line.<b>` (CUDA builds only; $<10^{-12}$ against CPU); see the Tests layer.
:::

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

The stub is the function-pointer type `hydro_ref_x1_fn` and the `DECLARE_DISPATCH` of `call_hydro_ref_x1` in
{{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.hpp hydro_ref_x1_fn >}}. The CPU kernel `hydro_ref_x1_cpu`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.cpp hydro_ref_x1_cpu >}}) dispatches on the floating-point type and parallelizes
over columns; the same file registers it for every CPU capability and registers the MPS implementation
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.cpp >}}). The CUDA kernel `hydro_ref_x1_cuda`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.cu hydro_ref_x1_cuda >}}) is registered in the same way at the end of its file.
Pointwise CUDA work uses the offsets of a `TensorIterator` in `gpu_kernel`
({{< code src/utils/loops.cuh gpu_kernel >}}). Line work uses `stencil_kernel`
({{< code src/utils/loops.cuh stencil_kernel >}}). The reconstruction switches to a tiled kernel when a line exceeds
1024 cells, and `recon_tile_width` ({{< code src/recon/recon_dispatch.cu recon_tile_width >}}) checks the index range,
the stencil shape and the 48 KiB shared-memory limit. The CMake option `CUDA` ({{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}) enables
the CUDA language, and the source list of the library adds the `.cu` files only in a CUDA build
({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}). The run-time device comes from the layout options (`LayoutOptionsImpl::from_yaml`,
{{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). Dispatch adds no truncation order; device agreement
needs a test per operator.

@fig-ch01-dispatch-flow shows the call sequence.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch01-dispatch-flow
#| fig-cap: "Dispatch tensor kernels by device. Labelled green boxes name operations or owners; black arrows show the reading sequence, not a timing measurement."
#| fig-alt: "Sequence: tensor device / dtype; dispatch stub; CPU columns | CUDA kernels; pointwise | line | tiled."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch01.figures.fig_dispatch_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

**Why a stub per kernel.** Three facts of the code.

1. A tensor operation follows its tensor's device, so only the hand-written kernels need a device choice; the stub
   declares that choice once per operation ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.hpp hydro_ref_x1_fn >}}).
2. Each device registers its own function against the stub ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.cpp >}},
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.cu hydro_ref_x1_cuda >}}); on a device without a registration the stub raises an
   error at the call.
3. The CUDA loops are shaped by the data: pointwise work over a `TensorIterator`, line work over one line per thread
   block, and a tiled kernel above 1024 cells. The tile must fit the 48 KiB shared-memory limit
   ({{< code src/recon/recon_dispatch.cu recon_tile_width >}}).

: Implementation anchors for device dispatch. {#tbl-ch01-dispatch-code}

1. Declare the operation: `hydro_ref_x1_fn` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.hpp hydro_ref_x1_fn >}}).
2. Implement and register per device: `hydro_ref_x1_cpu`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.cpp hydro_ref_x1_cpu >}}), `hydro_ref_x1_cuda`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.cu hydro_ref_x1_cuda >}}).
3. Loop shapes on CUDA: `gpu_kernel` ({{< code src/utils/loops.cuh gpu_kernel >}}), `stencil_kernel`
   ({{< code src/utils/loops.cuh stencil_kernel >}}), `recon_tile_width`
   ({{< code src/recon/recon_dispatch.cu recon_tile_width >}}).

**How to use it.** Build with CUDA and pick the device at launch:

```bash
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DNETCDF=ON -DUCX=OFF -DCUDA=ON   # the preface's line plus CUDA
cmake --build build --parallel 6                                           # compiles the .cu kernels
cd build/bin
DEVICE=cuda DEVICE_ID=0 ./straka.release straka_single.yaml   # the layout options read both variables
```

Refused: a kernel called on a device it has no registration for (an error from the dispatch stub), and `CUDA=ON`
with UCX[^rg-83fb6f9bc319] but without commux's CUDA sidecar ({{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}}; @sec-ch12-build). The stub and its declaration are these lines
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_dispatch.hpp hydro_ref_x1_fn >}}):

```cpp
using hydro_ref_x1_fn = void (*)(
    torch::Tensor const& w, torch::Tensor const& dx1f,
    torch::Tensor const& anchor, torch::Tensor const& psf_lo,
    torch::Tensor const& psf_hi, torch::Tensor const& pref,
    torch::Tensor const& dsf, torch::Tensor const& dref, int iu, double grav,
    bool uniform, bool phys_in, bool phys_out, bool wall_clamp);

DECLARE_DISPATCH(hydro_ref_x1_fn, call_hydro_ref_x1);
```

The type names the arguments every registered implementation must accept; the macro creates the stub that the
CPU, CUDA and MPS files register against.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_weno5_cuda_line.<b>` (registered in CUDA builds only) | CUDA and CPU reconstructions agree on lines of 32 to 1280 cells, in each direction | absolute $<10^{-12}$ | test constant |
| `test_coordinate.<b>` | the shared device and dtype parameter list runs each coordinate case | per assertion | a parameter list, not a tolerance |

: Source assertions for device dispatch. {#tbl-ch01-dispatch-tests}

The assertion is `expect_matches_cpu` ({{< code tests/test_weno5_cuda_line.cpp expect_matches_cpu >}}) in
{{< code tests/test_weno5_cuda_line.cpp recon_cuda.line_above_1024_matches_cpu >}}; the parameter list is the
`DeviceTest` fixture ({{< code tests/device_testing.hpp DeviceTest >}}).

The line test is registered only in a CUDA build and skips without a device; the coordinate test runs its CPU
cases always. Neither has been run for this report at the pin: **pending a pinned ctest run**. No report check
exists for this section.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The shared `DeviceTest` list has CPU and CUDA cases in float32 and float64; its MPS entry is commented out, and
a CUDA case skips when the build has no CUDA. Registrations alone are not test evidence; no CUDA or MPS
execution was performed for this chapter. The tiling test covers the reconstruction, not every other stencil
user.
:::
